podcast.title: Lieber & Stoller Collaboration
podcast.body: LeVern Baker was one of the "black performers" whom Jerry Lieber and Mike Stoller admired and recorded with almost exclusively for Atlantic Records. "And at the same time, they were also attached to Atlantic, where they were recording almost exclusively with the black performers that they admired, such as Ruth Brown, LeVern Baker and The Drifters."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Records with Mickey Baker
podcast.body: Mickey Baker contributed to records by LeVern Baker, indicating his widespread work as a session guitarist. "And records by Louis Jordan, LeVern Baker, Ray Charles and Moore."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Songs Closer to Jazz than Country
podcast.body: LeVern Baker's songs, alongside those of Ruth Brown and Dinah Washington, were characterized as being closer to jazz than to country music, making Janice Martin's interpretations with country instrumentation noteworthy. "The songs, Brown, Baker and Washington recorded were all closer to jazz than to country music."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
